# Design system — component usage guide

Generated documentation for AI and human consumers. One section per component.

## Avatar

Represents a user or entity.

A circular container that represents a person or entity — showing their image when available and falling back to initials otherwise. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg), can carry an optional online status dot, and binds its surface, text, and circular shape to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Represent a person or entity with an image or their initials; Show presence with the optional online status dot
**When not to use:** Displaying a decorative or brand image — use a plain image; As a button — wrap it in a Button or link if it must be interactive
**Do:** Provide meaningful alt text when showing a photo; Give a sensible initials fallback for when the image is missing; Keep initials to one or two characters
**Don't:** Don't rely on the status dot alone to convey presence — pair with text where it matters; Don't stretch non-square images — the image is cropped to a circle; Don't use an avatar as the only label for a person in dense UI without a name nearby
**Tokens:** color/bg/muted, color/text/primary, color/success/default, color/bg/canvas, radius/full, font/size/100, font/size/200, font/size/300

## Badge

Labels a status, count, or category.

A small pill-shaped label for short status, counts, or categories. It comes in four tones (default / secondary / destructive / outline), takes an optional leading icon, and binds its color, spacing, and full-radius shape to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Call out a status, state, or category — "Active", "Beta", "3 new"; Attach a short, at-a-glance label to another element
**When not to use:** Triggering an action — use a Button; A removable or selectable token in an input — use a Chip
**Do:** Keep the text to a word or two; Bind the color to a semantic tone that matches the meaning; Pair color with text or an icon so the meaning survives without color
**Don't:** Don't rely on color alone to convey status; Don't put an interactive control inside a badge — use a Button or Chip; Don't write full sentences — a badge is a label, not a message
**Tokens:** color/brand/primary, color/brand/onPrimary, color/bg/muted, color/text/primary, color/danger/default, color/danger/onDanger, color/border/default, radius/full, space/1, space/2, font/size/100

## Button

Triggers an action or event.

A clickable control that triggers an action — submitting a form, confirming a decision, or opening a dialog. It comes in six emphasis variants across three sizes, supports optional leading and trailing icons and a loading state, and binds every color, spacing, radius, and type value to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Trigger an action or event — submit, confirm, open a dialog; Give a view a single, clear primary action
**When not to use:** Navigating to another page or URL — use a Link (the link variant looks like a link but still triggers an action)
**Do:** Lead the label with a verb; Keep one primary (default) button per view; Keep labels short — about three words or fewer
**Don't:** Don't use a button for navigation — use a Link; Don't stack multiple primary buttons in one view; Don't disable a button without telling the user why
**Tokens:** color/brand/primary, color/brand/primaryHover, color/brand/primaryActive, color/brand/onPrimary, color/bg/muted, color/bg/mutedHover, color/bg/mutedActive, color/text/primary, color/focus/ring, color/focus/ringOnFill, radius/md, space/2, space/3, space/4, space/6, font/family/body, font/size/100, font/size/200, font/size/300, Focus Ring, Focus Ring On Fill

## Card

Groups related content and actions about a single subject.

A surface that groups related content and actions about one subject. It has two variants — default (bordered) and elevated (shadow) — and is built from composable parts (header, title, description, content, footer), with slots for an Avatar in the header and a Button in the footer. Background, border, radius, and elevation are bound to semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Group related content and actions about a single subject
**When not to use:** Primary page layout scaffolding; A bare list of text with no grouping
**Do:** Make the primary action obvious; Keep one main call-to-action per card
**Don't:** Don't nest cards more than one level deep; Don't make the whole card and an inner button separately clickable in conflicting ways
**Tokens:** color/bg/subtle, color/border/default, color/text/primary, color/text/secondary, radius/lg, space/1, space/2, space/3, space/4, space/6, font/family/heading, font/family/body, font/size/100, font/size/200, font/size/400

## Checkbox

Toggles an independent on/off choice.

A control for an independent on/off choice, rendered as a button with role="checkbox". It supports checked, unchecked, and indeterminate (a partial-selection dash) states across the full interaction set — default, hover, focus, active, and disabled — and binds its fill, border, radius, and focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Offer an independent on/off choice, like accepting terms; Select any number of options from a list (zero, one, or many); Represent a parent's partial selection with the indeterminate state
**When not to use:** Choosing exactly one option from a set — use a Radio group; A single setting that applies immediately with no Save — use a Switch
**Do:** Give every checkbox a visible, clickable label; Use the indeterminate state only for a parent summarizing mixed children; Group related checkboxes under a clear group label
**Don't:** Don't use a checkbox for a one-of-many choice — that's a Radio group; Don't use it for a setting that takes effect instantly — prefer a Switch; Don't leave the box unlabeled or rely on placement alone for meaning
**Tokens:** color/brand/primary, color/brand/primaryHover, color/brand/onPrimary, color/bg/canvas, color/border/default, color/border/strong, radius/sm, space/1, Focus Ring

## Input

Collects a single line of free-form text.

A single-line text field for free-form input. It comes in three sizes with default, focus, error, and disabled states, and an optional leading icon. Border, background, radius, and type are bound to semantic tokens; the focus state uses the focus-ring and border/focus tokens and the error state uses the danger tokens.

**When to use:** Collect a single line of free-form text — a name, email, or search query
**When not to use:** Choosing from a fixed set of options — use Select or Radio; Long, multi-line text — use Textarea
**Do:** Always pair the field with a visible label; Show format hints as helper text; Reserve space for error text to avoid layout shift
**Don't:** Don't use placeholder text as the only label; Don't validate on every keystroke before the first blur
**Tokens:** color/bg/subtle, color/bg/muted, color/border/default, color/border/focus, color/border/strong, color/border/subtle, color/danger/default, color/focus/ring, color/text/secondary, radius/md, space/2, space/3, space/4, font/family/body, font/size/100, font/size/200, font/size/300, Focus Ring

## Radio

Selects one option from a set.

A control for choosing exactly one option from a set, rendered as a button with role="radio" and coordinated by a RadioGroup wrapper that holds the selected value. Each radio shows selected or unselected across the full interaction set — default, hover, focus, active, and disabled — and binds its border, brand inner dot, circular shape, and focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Choose exactly one option from a small, visible set of choices; Present mutually exclusive options where seeing them all matters
**When not to use:** Selecting more than one option — use Checkboxes; Choosing from a long list — use a Select to save space
**Do:** Wrap radios in a RadioGroup with a clear group label; Give each radio a visible, clickable label; Preselect a sensible default when one clearly applies
**Don't:** Don't use a radio group to allow multiple selections — use Checkboxes; Don't offer a single lone radio — that choice can't be deselected; use a Checkbox; Don't split one logical choice across multiple groups
**Tokens:** color/brand/primary, color/border/default, color/text/primary, radius/full, space/2, font/size/200, Focus Ring

## Select

Chooses one option from a dropdown list.

An accessible trigger for choosing one option from a list, wrapping a native select so it inherits the platform's open/close and keyboard behavior. A non-interactive chevron sits on the trailing edge. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg) with default, focus, error, and disabled states, and binds its background, border, radius, and focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Choose a single option from a moderate-to-long list; Save vertical space when a Radio group would be too many options
**When not to use:** A short set of a few options that benefit from being visible — use Radios; Selecting more than one value — use a multi-select or checkboxes
**Do:** Always pair with a visible label; Order options predictably (alphabetical, or by frequency); Provide a clear default or an unselected placeholder option
**Don't:** Don't use a Select for only two or three visible options — use Radios; Don't hide critical actions inside a Select — it's for choosing values; Don't rely on the placeholder as the field's only label
**Tokens:** color/bg/subtle, color/text/primary, color/text/muted, color/border/default, color/danger/default, radius/md, space/3, space/4, font/size/200, font/size/300, Focus Ring

## Select Menu

The dropdown surface that holds selectable options.

The popover surface opened from a Select trigger — a bordered, elevated panel with role="listbox" that holds a list of Select Menu Items passed as its content. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg) and binds its surface, border, radius, and elevation to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Present the list of options opened from a Select trigger; Group a set of Select Menu Items into one scrollable, elevated surface
**When not to use:** A menu of actions or commands — use a Menu, not a listbox; Free-form text entry — use an Input or Textarea
**Do:** Fill it with Select Menu Items and keep them consistently sized; Match the menu size to the Select trigger that opens it; Let long lists scroll rather than overflowing the surface
**Don't:** Don't mix unrelated actions into an option listbox; Don't nest another menu surface inside a single option; Don't hardcode its elevation or radius — they come from tokens
**Tokens:** color/bg/canvas, color/text/primary, color/border/subtle, radius/md, space/1, Elevation

## Select Menu Item

One selectable row inside a Select Menu.

A single selectable option within a Select Menu, rendered with role="option". Its label is passed as content and a trailing check appears when it is the current selection. It covers the full interaction set — default, hover, focused (keyboard navigation), selected, and disabled — and binds its text, surfaces, and the selected check to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Represent one choosable option inside a Select Menu listbox; Mark the currently selected value with the trailing check
**When not to use:** A clickable action or command — use a Menu item, not an option; Standalone outside a Select Menu — items only make sense within the listbox
**Do:** Keep option labels short and scannable; Let the trailing check be the single, consistent selected indicator; Keep items visually uniform within one menu
**Don't:** Don't put multiple interactive controls inside one option row; Don't convey selection by color alone — the check carries it too; Don't use an option row for an action — that belongs in a Menu
**Tokens:** color/text/primary, color/text/disabled, color/bg/subtle, color/bg/muted, color/border/focus, color/brand/primary, radius/sm, space/2, space/3, font/size/200

## Spinner

Indicates that something is loading.

A continuously spinning loader that signals an indeterminate wait — an action in progress or a region still loading. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg), takes its color from the foreground token, and exposes an accessible "Loading" status to assistive technology.

**When to use:** Signal that an action is in progress — a button submitting, a panel fetching; Fill a region that is still loading when you can't show real content yet
**When not to use:** Showing how far along a known task is — use a determinate progress bar; Long or content-heavy loads where a skeleton better previews the layout
**Do:** Give the spinner an accessible label so screen readers announce the wait; Match the size to its context — small inside controls, larger for regions; Pair a longer wait with a short message so users know what's happening
**Don't:** Don't use a spinner for progress you can actually measure; Don't leave a spinner running with no resolution or timeout; Don't rely on the spin alone — expose a text status for assistive tech
**Tokens:** color/text/primary, space/2, space/3, space/4

## Switch

Toggles a single setting on or off.

A toggle for a single on/off setting that takes effect immediately, rendered as a button with role="switch". The track fills with the brand color when on and a muted color when off, with an adaptive thumb whose visible edge is carried by a strong border. It covers off, on, and disabled states and binds every color and the focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.

**When to use:** Turn a single setting on or off with an immediate effect; Offer a binary preference that doesn't need a separate Save
**When not to use:** A choice that only applies after submitting a form — use a Checkbox; Choosing one of several options — use a Radio group
**Do:** Use a clear label that reads as an on/off state; Apply the change immediately when toggled; Keep the label stable — don't relabel the switch as it flips
**Don't:** Don't require a separate Save for a switch — that's a Checkbox pattern; Don't use a switch for non-binary choices; Don't rely on the thumb position alone — pair with a visible label
**Tokens:** color/brand/primary, color/bg/muted, color/bg/canvas, color/border/strong, radius/full, space/1, Focus Ring

## Textarea

Collects multi-line free-form text.

The multi-line sibling of Input: a styled native textarea that fills its container, grows vertically as needed, and shares Input's token-driven border, background, and focus ring. It covers default, focus, error, and disabled states and can flag invalid input with a destructive border and ring.

**When to use:** Collect longer, multi-line free-form text — comments, descriptions, notes; Give users room to write more than a single line comfortably
**When not to use:** A single line of text — use an Input; Choosing from a fixed set of options — use a Select or Radio group
**Do:** Always pair with a visible label; Show format or length hints as helper text; Reserve space for error text to avoid layout shift
**Don't:** Don't use placeholder text as the only label; Don't validate on every keystroke before the first blur; Don't fix the height so short that users can't see what they wrote
**Tokens:** color/bg/subtle, color/text/primary, color/text/muted, color/border/default, color/danger/default, radius/md, space/3, font/size/300, Focus Ring

## Tooltip

Shows a brief hint on hover or focus.

A lightweight text hint that reveals on hover or keyboard focus of its trigger. It can be placed on any of four sides (top / right / bottom / left) with an arrow pointing back to the trigger, and binds its surface, text, radius, and elevation to the system's semantic tokens. Because it reveals on focus, the trigger must itself be focusable.

**When to use:** Add a short, supplementary hint to a control — what an icon button does; Clarify a label or value without taking up permanent space
**When not to use:** Essential information a user must not miss — put it inline; Rich or interactive content — use a Popover instead
**Do:** Keep the text short — a phrase, not a paragraph; Attach the tooltip to a focusable trigger so keyboard users get it too; Use it for supplementary hints, not essential instructions
**Don't:** Don't hide essential information only inside a tooltip; Don't put links, buttons, or form fields inside — use a Popover; Don't attach a tooltip to a non-focusable element — keyboard users can't reach it
**Tokens:** color/bg/muted, color/text/primary, radius/md, space/1, space/2, font/size/200, Elevation
